name: HiGS (Hierarchically Tiled Gaussian Splatting)
aliases: Hierarchical Rendering Architecture for Real-Time 3D Gaussian Splatting
definition: HiGS is a rendering architecture that decouples partitioning from rasterization granularity by using a two-scale spatial hierarchy. It resolves the tile-size trade-off in 3DGS where partitioning favors large tiles (fewer pairs) and rasterization favors small tiles (less wasted work). HiGS performs binning and depth-sorting at a coarse macro-tile granularity while rasterizing at a fine render-tile granularity.
summary: HiGS is a rendering architecture for 3D Gaussian Splatting that decouples spatial partitioning from rasterization granularity using a two-scale hierarchy to balance load and eliminate rasterizer tail effects.
